title: SlotBand credits: hybrid reserved-burst packaging & autoscale SLA experiments
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Proposal: introduce a SlotBand packaging tier that blends reserved GPU slot commitments with time-limited burst credits and an autoscale elasticity curve. The goal is to reduce churn for mid-enterprise customers (typical 13-25% monthly growth) by giving predictable base throughput plus headroom for spiky traffic while preserving clear SLA bands and simple contract language for legal/SQ. This ticket drives the experiment design, pricing models, contract language samples for the security questionnaire, and the telemetry signals required to validate economics and reliability.
acceptance_criteria: Define 3 SlotBand plans (Base, Base+Burst, Premium with guaranteed lanes) with pricing model and sample contract clauses
Run pricing sensitivity simulation on 50 historical customer traces and produce expected monthly cost delta vs existing reserve-only plans
Implement experiment flags in Console UI for 10 pilot customers and measure adoption, burst utilization, and SLOs over 30 days
Legal/SQ sign-off on sample contract and completed security questionnaire draft for slot-based entitlements
Post-experiment go/no-go decision documented with recommended rollout cadence and merchant billing changes
comments: 2026-02-18 Aisha Patel: Kickoff meeting notes attached. Alignment with sales on target personas (AI SaaS, media generation). Agreed to keep three simple SKUs: SlotBand-Base, SlotBand-Burst, SlotBand-Premium. Action: PM to produce initial pricing bands and simulation inputs by 2026-02-25. Links: https://drive.redwood.example/SlotBand/kickoff-notes (Confluence/Drive draft).

2026-02-22 Marco Nguyen: Initial pricing model posted. Model assumptions: slot = 1 GPU-equivalent throughput unit (avg 2000 tokens/min for batch workloads), burst credits redeemable across region within 48h, unused credits expire monthly. Shared spreadsheet: https://sheets.redwood.example/pricing-model-PM-45712. Feedback requested from Revenue Ops and Finance.

2026-02-24 Revenue Ops (Lena Ortiz): Concern: burst credits complicate invoice reconciliation for enterprise billing. Proposed solution: show reserved hours and burst consumption on invoice line items and give a month-end detailed usage CSV. Action: ENG to add usage export fields (dependency ENG-1842).

2026-02-25 Data Science (Ravi Mehta): Ran consumption simulation on 50 anonymized customer traces. Key result: SlotBand-Base reduces expected cost volatility by ~22% for customers with <30% monthly peak ratio; adding Burst credits cuts overage events by 68%. Uploaded analysis: https://dashboards.redwood.example/simulations/slotband-50trace-2026-02-25.

2026-02-27 Compliance review (Nadia Chen): Security questionnaire draft included new entitlement section that maps slot-level access to existing RBAC. Requirements: (1) encrypt slot assignment metadata at rest, (2) audit logs per-burst redemption event. Added to security checklist. Link to draft SQ: https://confluence.redwood.example/sq/slotband-draft-2026-02-27.

2026-02-28 Design review (Harper Lee): Console UX mockups for purchase flow and burst consumption meter reviewed. Feedback: present burst as "credit buffer" not "minutes" to reduce confusion; add a time-to-replenish indicator for autoscale. Figma link: https://figma.redwood.example/file/SlotBand/UI-v1.

2026-02-28 Engineering sync (Marco Nguyen): Agreed scope for pilot: server-side flags to enable slot accounting, a light-weight quota ledger for burst credits, and expanded telemetry for p95/p99 latency by slot. ENG tasks split across runtime batching team and billing team. Depended on ENG-1842 for usage export and ENG-40321 for quota ledger. Timeline estimate: 4 sprints for minimal viable pilot infra.

2026-03-01 PM note (Aisha Patel): Updated plan after Finance and Legal feedback. Two open trade-offs: (A) How strict should premption be when autoscale exceeds reserved+burst? Option 1 = soft-preempt (throttle <5%), Option 2 = hard-preempt (queue/cancel). Sales prefers soft-preempt to avoid user-visible failures; infra prefers deterministic capping. Vote: Keep soft-preempt for pilot, instrument errors, then revisit. (B) Pricing granularity: hourly billing vs daily metered buckets. Finance favors daily buckets to simplify invoicing; Pilot uses daily aggregation. Documented decision and next steps in PRD: https://confluence.redwood.example/prd/slotband-2026-03-01.

2026-03-01 Legal (Erin Wells): Draft contract clause for reserved slot commitments and burst credits attached. Clause outlines rolling 12-month commitment with monthly reconciliation and explicit termination language for overage disputes. Requested to include SOC2 control mappings and explicit KMS usage notes for slot metadata encryption. Added to security_review_required. Draft: https://drive.redwood.example/contracts/slotband-draft-2026-03-01.pdf.
